2026-04-15T10:38:08.115000000-0400	10.10.0.1	10.10.1.10	445	51004	True

--- SYN followed by RST/ACK ---
# Filter: tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.flags.ack == 1 && tcp.flags.reset == 1
# tshark -r lateral_movement.pcap -Y tcp.flags.syn == 1 && tcp.flags.ack == 1 && tcp.flags.reset == 1 -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.srcport -e tcp.dstport

--- Kerberos errors ---
# Filter: kerberos.error_code
# tshark -r lateral_movement.pcap -Y kerberos.error_code -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e kerberos.error_code

--- SMB status/error responses ---
# Filter: smb2.nt_status || smb.nt_status
# tshark -r lateral_movement.pcap -Y smb2.nt_status || smb.nt_status -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e smb2.nt_status -e smb.nt_status

Failure interpretation:
- TCP RST indicates that a TCP connection was reset.
- SYN followed by RST/ACK indicates that the attempted TCP service connection was refused/reset at that point.
- Kerberos error codes indicate a Kerberos-level error when present.
- SMB NT status values indicate the status returned by the SMB operation when visible.
- No conclusion about attacker intent is made from a failure alone.
